text:
THE KENYA NATIONAL EXAMINATIONS COUNCIL
 SCHOOL BASED ASSESSMENT
 Grade 7 2023
 1. HEALTH EDUCATION PRACTICAL SECTION
 SCORE GRID
 Question Practical
 Maximum Score 25
 Learner’s Score
Instructions to learners
(a) This paper consists of two sections, with a task in each section: a practical task and a project
 task.
(b) Both tasks are scored out of 25 marks.
 This paper consists of 5 printed pages.
 Learners should check the question paper to ascertain that all the
 pages are printed as indicated.
 ©2023 The Kenya National Examinations Council: Grade 7 Health Education 1
 INSTRUCTIONS TO SCHOOLS
 (a) This section consists of one performance task on carrying out First Aid on a fractured limb.
 The teacher to:
(b) guide learners on how to source for information on common causes of accidents and injuries in the
 community, how to carry out First Aid on a fractured limb and write short notes on the same,
(c) guide learners in identifying and collecting appropriate materials needed to undertake the First Aid
 activity,
(d) encourage learners to share materials needed for the activity,
(e) encourage learners to improvise equipment and materials for the task where possible.
 Purchasing commercial First Aid kits and equipment for this task is highly discouraged,
(f) supervise learners and ensure that they observe safety while carrying out the task,
(g) ensure that learners are dressed appropriately for the activity for safety and hygiene,
(h) organize learners in pairs and ensure they take turns in performing the task,
(i) ensure learners clear and tidy up the working area,
(j) guide learners to reflect on the entire project to establish achievements and areas of improvement for
 future tasks,
(k) use the scoring guide provided to assess the learners as they carry out the task.
 TASK: CARRYING OUT FIRST AID ON A FRACTURED LIMB: LEG OR ARM
1.0. Before the day of assessment,
 learners:
 1.1 search for information from multiple sources on the common causes of accidents and injuries
 in the community,
 1.2 how to carry out First Aid on a fractured leg or arm,
 1.3 share in pairs the information on the common causes of accidents and injuries in
 the community and how to carry out First Aid on a fractured leg or arm,
 1.4 decide to carry out First Aid either on a fractured leg or arm,
 1.5 in pairs:
 (i) write the procedure to follow while carrying out First Aid on a fractured leg or arm,
 (ii) identify materials needed to carry out the First Aid,
 (iii) discuss safety precautions to observe while carrying out the First Aid.
2.0. On the day of assessment,
 ©2023 The Kenya National Examinations Council: Grade 7 Health Education 2
learners:
 2.1. bring materials required for the First Aid activity,
 2.3. in pairs set up the working area,
 2.4. in pairs take turns to carry out the First Aid activity,
 2.5 reflect on the entire practical activity to establish achievements and areas of
 improvement for future activities
3.0. On the day of assessment,
the teacher to:
 3.1 check the procedure written by learners on how to carry out First Aid before
 learners commence the activity and guide as appropriate.
 3.2. observe, assess and award scores using the scoring guide
 provided as learners:
 (i) prepare a working area for carrying out the First Aid activity,
 (ii) carry out the First Aid in turns,
 (iii) tidy up the working area,
 (iv) safely dispose of the used First Aid materials.
 3.3. ask learners to reflect on the entire practical activity to establish achievements and areas of
 improvement for future activities,
 3.4. score learners independently based on ability of the individual learner to
 demonstrate the skill during the activity.
 3.5. be as objective as possible when awarding the scores.

 2. HEALTH EDUCATION GRADE 7 PROJECT
INSTRUCTIONS TO THE TEACHER
(a) This section consists of one performance task: Preparing a health promotional material to:
 i) create awareness on a common health concern in the community,
 ii) promote individual and community wellness.
b) The teacher to organize learners in groups of up to 6.
c) The teacher to guide learners to keep a journal of the progress of the project.
d) The teacher to guide learners to source for information from multiple sources such as textbooks, resource
persons, parents or guardians, digital devices and the internet and make short notes on:
 i) common health concerns in the community
 ii) how to prepare health promotional materials.
e) The teacher to guide learners in selecting appropriate resources for carrying out the project.
f) The teacher to encourage learners to share resources where applicable.
g) The teacher to encourage learners to use locally available resources as much as possible as they make the
health promotional materials.
h) The teacher to ensure that learners observe safety measures and precautions while undertaking the project.
i) The teacher to guide learners to display their finished products and explain how the messages promote
individual and community wellness for healthy living.
j) The teacher to guide learners to distribute and share health promotional materials to the school community
k) The teacher to guide learners to reflect on the entire project to establish achievements and areas of
improvement for future projects.
l) The teacher to use the scoring guide provided to assess group performance of the project
m) The teacher to use the group’s score as the individual learner’s score.
n) The teacher to enter the individual learner’s score as project marks in the score sheet provided.
o) The teacher to enter the project marks in the assessment sheet in the scoring guide and upload the scores by
11th August 2023.
NOTE: AB for the learner who did not participate in the project.
 ©2023 The Kenya National Examinations Council: Grade 7 Health Education 4
PERFORMANCE TASK
Assuming there is a rising health concern in your community that requires members of the public to be made
aware of and have the concern addressed, prepare health promotional materials to:
 i) create awareness on the common health concern in the community,
 ii) promote individual and community wellness for healthy living.
To perform the task, the learner should:
a) source for information from multiple sources such as textbooks, resource persons, parents or guardians,
digital devices and the internet on:
 i) common health concerns in the community
 ii) how to prepare health promotional materials.
b) take short notes on common health concerns in the community and how to prepare health promotional
materials.
c) share information collected and discuss common health concerns in the community and how to prepare
health promotional materials.
d) select their preferred health promotional material to make.
e) identify suitable locally available resources they will require to make the selected health promotional
material.
f) make health promotional materials using the locally available resources identified.
g) display the finished product (health promotional material) in the classroom.
h) take a gallery walk to observe their peers’ work, comment and make suggestions for improvement.
i) orally explain how the message contained in the health promotional material creates awareness on a
common health concern in the community to promote wellness of individual and community.
j) distribute and share the health promotional materials with the rest of the school community.
k) keep a journal to show progress of the project.
l) reflect on the entire project to establish achievements and areas of improvement.
